In recent years, a new trend has become common in branding: everyday products such as food, drinks and even tools are given human features, like smiling faces and simple arms and legs.
Compared with more serious or formal designs, these playful images can make people feel relaxed.
As a result, such designs are accepted by people of different ages and are widely used in different industries, from food to fashion.
In some cases, companies even rely on ready-made templates (模版) instead of original ideas.
As a result, different brands may begin to look alike, making it harder for consumers to tell them apart.
The key issue, therefore, is how such designs can be used in a more creative way, rather than simply copied.
